item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00396","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C01","C15","C24"],"selected_candidate_label":"C01","confidence":0.78,"relationship_type":"structural_functional_template","rationale":"C01 provides a concrete drafting pattern closely mirrored by the child: a letter to a committee chairman advocating pending legislation, explaining that an alternative administrative or quasi-administrative route remains available if Congress does not act, and emphasizing that the legislative route is preferable despite that fallback. C15 is highly relevant to the specific lead-and-zinc factual background but is less similar as a drafting structure. C24 parallels the combination of domestic-industry distress, Tariff Commission action, and commitment to expanded foreign trade, but not the child's central legislation-versus-fallback sequence.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"It is understood, of course, that the initiation before the Tariff Commission of an escape clause proceeding by the industry is available in the last instance... if the Congress does not pass the requested legislation.","parent_excerpt":"In order to build these works, if the Congress does not enact the legislation now before it... it will be necessary for the United States and Canada jointly to apply to the International Joint Commission.","explanation":"Both identify a specific alternative commission-based procedure that will be used if Congress fails to enact the preferred legislation."},{"child_excerpt":"The special circumstances of this case that suggest the desirability of following the legislative route...","parent_excerpt":"The best, the simplest, and the quickest way to get them is through legislation by the Congress.","explanation":"Both frame congressional legislation as the preferred route even though another mechanism is legally or practically available."},{"child_excerpt":"In that event, I would request the Tariff Commission to expedite its consideration of the matter.","parent_excerpt":"In order to lose no time if the Congress does not act... the application to the International Joint Commission will be completed and filed at an early date.","explanation":"The fallback is paired with an assurance of prompt action, reinforcing the same operative sequence."}]}
